skill.name: skill-standardization
skill.description: Standardize and validate SKILL.md files against the Agent Skills specification. Use when creating, auditing, or improving skills for reliable activation and consistent structure.
skill.summary: Validate and standardize Agent Skill files for compliant structure and reliable triggering.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Context review found that the static findings are false positives from shell arithmetic, fixed local parsing commands, Markdown backticks, and documentation links. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, unsafe network behavior, or arbitrary command execution was found in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: check "error" "Name format: invalid characters or leading/trailing hyphen: '$name'"
- Adding evaluation test cases (`evals/evals.json`) to a skill
| `name` | Yes | 1–64 chars, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphe
| `description` | Yes | 1–1024 chars, must describe what skill does AND when to trigger |
| `allowed-tools` | No | Space-delimited list of pre-approved tools |
| `license` | No | License name or reference to bundled file |
| `metadata` | No | Arbitrary key-value map for additional fields |
- `name` format: lowercase, no consecutive hyphens, matches directory name
The `description` field determines when a skill triggers. A weak description means the skill never a
| `## Purpose` | `## When to use this skill` |
| `## When to Use` | `## When to use this skill` |
- **`scripts/validate_skill.sh`** — Validates a SKILL.md against the Agent Skills spec
2. **Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines** — move detailed reference docs to `references/`
3. **Pin script versions** — use `uvx ruff@0.8.0` not just `ruff` to ensure reproducibility
Good assertions are **verifiable**: file exists, JSON is valid, chart has 3 bars. Avoid vague assert

content.value_statement: Skill files can drift from the Agent Skills specification and trigger unreliably. This skill validates structure, frontmatter, descriptions, and evaluation examples.
actual_capabilities: Validates SKILL.md frontmatter fields such as name, description, allowed-tools, and compatibility.
Checks name format, directory-name matching, description length, and trigger phrasing.
Reports missing recommended sections including examples, best practices, and references.
Provides templates for new SKILL.md files and evals/evals.json test cases.
Runs batch validation for skill directories that contain SKILL.md files.
limitations: The shell validator uses grep, sed, and awk parsing rather than a full YAML parser.
It cannot prove that a description will always trigger correctly in every agent client.
It does not perform deep security scanning of scripts or referenced resources.
It depends on local filesystem access and a POSIX shell.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Skill for Publishing
use_cases.description: Validate structure, required frontmatter, and recommended sections before submitting a skill.

use_cases.title: Audit a Skill Repository
use_cases.description: Batch-check many skill directories and collect errors and warnings for cleanup.

use_cases.title: Improve Skill Activation
use_cases.description: Rewrite descriptions so agents understand capabilities, trigger conditions, and related user wording.

prompt_templates.title: Validate One Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill-standardization to check the skill in <path>. Summarize errors, warnings, and recommended edits.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Review <path>/SKILL.md. Rewrite the frontmatter description to explain capabilities, trigger conditions, and synonyms while staying under 1024 characters.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Legacy Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from older skill formats.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the skill at <path> to standard Agent Skills structure. Preserve intent, normalize headings, and add missing recommended sections.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Release Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Batch validate all skills under <path>. Prioritize blocking errors, description quality, eval coverage, and scripts that need manual review.

output_examples.output: A concise report lists required field status, section coverage, description length, and the edits needed before release.

output_examples.input: Improve the trigger description for a spreadsheet skill.
output_examples.output: A revised description states the supported spreadsheet tasks, when to use the skill, and related phrases users may type.

output_examples.input: Batch audit every skill in a repository.
output_examples.output: A repository-level summary separates blocking errors from warnings and identifies which skill directories need updates.

best_practices: Run validation before publishing or changing a skill description.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move long reference material to separate resources.
Add evaluation prompts that match real user requests and expected outcomes.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague descriptions that only name the domain.
Do not hide required trigger details in references instead of frontmatter.
Do not rely on interactive scripts because agent shells may be non-interactive.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It checks SKILL.md frontmatter, naming rules, description quality, recommended sections, and file length.

faq.question: Can it create a new skill file?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a standard SKILL.md template and guidance for required sections.

faq.question: Does it support batch validation?
faq.answer: Yes. The included script can validate every skill directory under a selected parent directory.

faq.question: Does it fully parse YAML?
faq.answer: No. The validator uses shell text tools, so complex YAML should be reviewed manually.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for Claude Code and compatible agent clients with filesystem access.

faq.question: Does it perform security review?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on specification compliance and structure, not deep security scanning.
